name: google-maps/directions
description: Get Google Maps directions between two places by car, transit, walking, cycling or flight, with routes, distance, duration and step-by-step instructions.

gl.description: Parameter defines the country to use for the Google search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France) Head to the Google countries page for a full list of supported Google countries.

hl.description: Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Maps Directions search. It's a two or three-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French), optionally followed by a two-letter or three-digit region code (e.g., `en-gb` for British English, or `es-419` for Latin American Spanish). Head to the Google languages page for a full list of supported Google languages.

time.description: Parameter defines the time to travel. Available options: `depart_at:xxxxxx` - Specifies the departure time, where `xxxxxx` is the timestamp. E.g. `depart_at:1698229538` specifies the departure time to 2023-10-25 10:25:38 GMT+0000 `arrive_by:xxxxxx` - Specifies the arrival time, where `xxxxxx` is the timestamp. E.g. `arrive_by:1698229538` specifies the arrival time to 2023-10-25 10:25:38 GMT+0000 `last_available` - Takes the last available transit. This option works only if `travel_mode` parameter is set to: `3` (Transit)

avoid.description: Parameter defines avoid options. Available options: `highways` - Highways `tolls` - Tolls `ferries` - Ferries You can also combine multiple options by joining them with a comma (e.g.: `highways,tolls`).

route.description: Parameter defines route options. Available options: `2` - Fewer transfers `3` - Less walking `4` - Wheelchair accessible Parameter works only if `travel_mode` parameter is set to: `3` (Transit)

prefer.description: Parameter defines preferred transit options. Available options: `bus` - Bus `subway` - Subway `train` - Train `tram_light_rail` - Tram and light rail You can also combine multiple options by joining them with a comma (e.g.: `subway,train`). Parameter works only if `travel_mode` parameter is set to: `3` (Transit)

end_addr.description: Parameter defines the address of the ending point for the direction you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Maps Directions search. Alternatively, you can use `end_data_id` or `end_coords`.

end_coords.description: Parameter defines the GPS coordinates of the ending point for the direction you want to search. The format is `latitude,longitude`. E.g. `30.197471099,-97.66635289`. Alternatively, you can use `end_addr` or `end_data_id`.

start_addr.description: Parameter defines the address of the starting point for the direction you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Maps Directions search. Alternatively, you can use `start_data_id` or `start_coords`.

end_data_id.description: Parameter defines the data ID of the ending point for the direction you want to search. Find the data ID of a place using our Google Maps API. Alternatively, you can use `end_addr` or `end_coords`.

travel_mode.description: Parameter defines the travel mode. Available options: `6` - Best (Default) `0` - Driving `9` - Two-wheeler `3` - Transit `2` - Walking `1` - Cycling `4` - Flight

start_coords.description: Parameter defines the GPS coordinates of the starting point for the direction you want to search. The format is `latitude,longitude`. E.g. `30.197471099,-97.66635289`. Alternatively, you can use `start_addr` or `start_data_id`.

distance_unit.description: Parameter defines the displayed distance unit. Available options: `1` - miles `0` - km

# Google Maps Directions

Get Google Maps directions between two places by car, transit, walking, cycling or flight, with routes, distance, duration and step-by-step instructions.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/google-maps/directions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"start_addr": "Austin-Bergstrom International Airport", "end_addr": "Texas State Capitol"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data` as structured JSON.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start_addr` | string | No | Parameter defines the address of the starting point for the direction you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Maps Directions search. Alternatively, you can use `start_data_id` or `start_coords`. |
| `end_addr` | string | No | Parameter defines the address of the ending point for the direction you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Maps Directions search. Alternatively, you can use `end_data_id` or `end_coords`. |
| `gl` | string | No | Parameter defines the country to use for the Google search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France) Head to the Google countries page for a full list of supported Googl |
| `hl` | string | No | Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Maps Directions search. It's a two or three-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French), optionally followed by a two-letter or three-digit region |
| `travel_mode` | string | No | Parameter defines the travel mode. Available options: `6` - Best (Default) `0` - Driving `9` - Two-wheeler `3` - Transit `2` - Walking `1` - Cycling `4` - Flight |
| `start_data_id` | string | No | Parameter defines the data ID of the starting point for the direction you want to search. Find the data ID of a place using our Google Maps API. Alternatively, you can use `start_addr` or `start_coords`. |
| `end_data_id` | string | No | Parameter defines the data ID of the ending point for the direction you want to search. Find the data ID of a place using our Google Maps API. Alternatively, you can use `end_addr` or `end_coords`. |
| `start_coords` | string | No | Parameter defines the GPS coordinates of the starting point for the direction you want to search. The format is `latitude,longitude`. E.g. `30.197471099,-97.66635289`. Alternatively, you can use `start_addr` or `start_data_id`. |
| `end_coords` | string | No | Parameter defines the GPS coordinates of the ending point for the direction you want to search. The format is `latitude,longitude`. E.g. `30.197471099,-97.66635289`. Alternatively, you can use `end_addr` or `end_data_id`. |
| `distance_unit` | string | No | Parameter defines the displayed distance unit. Available options: `1` - miles `0` - km |
| `avoid` | string | No | Parameter defines avoid options. Available options: `highways` - Highways `tolls` - Tolls `ferries` - Ferries You can also combine multiple options by joining them with a comma (e.g.: `highways,tolls`). |
| `prefer` | string | No | Parameter defines preferred transit options. Available options: `bus` - Bus `subway` - Subway `train` - Train `tram_light_rail` - Tram and light rail You can also combine multiple options by joining them with a comma (e.g.: `subway,train`). |
| `route` | string | No | Parameter defines route options. Available options: `2` - Fewer transfers `3` - Less walking `4` - Wheelchair accessible Parameter works only if `travel_mode` parameter is set to: `3` (Transit) |
| `time` | string | No | Parameter defines the time to travel. Available options: `depart_at:xxxxxx` - Specifies the departure time, where `xxxxxx` is the timestamp. E.g. `depart_at:1698229538` specifies the departure time to 2023-10-25 10:25:38 GMT+0000 `arrive_by |
| `json_restrictor` | string | No | Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details. |
